Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

all adjective and pronoun

every one of, the whole number of

also all of, all of them, all of us, all together, not all

classical

Verg. Ecl. 8.63: nōn omnia possumus omnēs
Liv. 21.54.5: ut prandēre omnēs jubērent
Traupman 270

omnis, omne

adjective, third declension; in the plural, all (people, things)

all; in the singular, every

In the plural, “all”: omnēs, all (people), omnia, all (things) (see everyone, everything). In the singular it is “every” (see every), or all of a kind or a mass: omne forum, all the square (Prud. Perist. 3.177). For all of one thing taken whole, Latin prefers tōtus.

Other words

  • tōtus, tōta, tōtum — all (of one thing), the whole

    adjective; gen. tōtīus, dat. tōtī, declension · also used · classical · Mart. 13.52.1: tōta quidem pōnātur anas; Plin. Ep. 7.3.2: līber tōtus diēs

    One thing, all of it: tōta domus, all the house; with a word of time, “all … long”: tōtum diem (see whole).

  • cūnctī, cūnctae, cūncta — all together, all of them

    adjective, mostly plural (cūnctus, cūncta, cūnctum), declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 5.70: cūnctī adsint; Cic. Fam. 4.4.3: cūnctus senātus (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: from conjūnctus, “all in a body, all together”, the members thought of as joined.

  • ūniversī, ūniversae, ūniversa — all together, all at once

    adjective, mostly plural (ūniversus, ūniversa, ūniversum), declension · also used · classical · Tac. Agr. 12.2: ita singulī pugnant, ūniversī vincuntur

    All at once, as one body, as against singulī, one by one.

Examples

  • nōn omnia possumus omnēs

    we can’t all do everythingVerg. Ecl. 8.63

  • ut prandēre omnēs jubērent

    to order all the men to have their mealLiv. 21.54.5

  • eadem omnibus pōnō

    I serve the same to allPlin. Ep. 2.6.3

  • ecce nivem glaciālis hiems ingerit et tegit omne forum

    look, icy winter is heaping up snow and covering all the squarePrud. Perist. 3.176–177

  • ita singulī pugnant, ūniversī vincuntur

    so they fight one at a time and are beaten all togetherTac. Agr. 12.2

  • “Sophōs!” ūniversī clāmāmus

    “Bravo!” we all shout togetherPetr. 40.1

See also every, each, everyone, everything, whole, one of.
